17	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation;
18	
19	import java.time.LocalDate;
20	
21	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
22	
23	/**
24	 * Enforces that no more than {@value #MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY} owners may be registered on a single day.
25	 * The owners already registered today are counted by their registration date via
26	 * {@link DailyRegistrationCounter}; once that count reaches the cap, no further owner may be created
27	 * until the next day.
28	 */
29	@Component
30	public class DailyRegistrationCapacityValidator {
31	
32	    /** The maximum number of owners that may be registered in a single day. */
33	    public static final long MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY = 100;
34	
35	    private final DailyRegistrationCounter dailyRegistrationCounter;
36	
37	    public DailyRegistrationCapacityValidator(DailyRegistrationCounter dailyRegistrationCounter) {
38	        this.dailyRegistrationCounter = dailyRegistrationCounter;
39	    }
40	
41	    /**
42	     * Rejects an owner registration once {@value #MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY} or more owners have already
43	     * been registered on the given day.
44	     *
45	     * @param day the (business) day the owner is being registered on
46	     * @throws DailyRegistrationLimitExceededException if that day is already at capacity
47	     */
48	    public void validateHasCapacity(LocalDate day) {
49	        if (this.dailyRegistrationCounter.count(day) >= MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY) {
50	            throw new DailyRegistrationLimitExceededException(MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY);
51	        }
52	    }
53	}

18	
19	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service.ClinicService;
20	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
21	
22	/**
23	 * Counts how many existing owners live in a given city, compared case-insensitively. The
24	 * comparison is done in memory because the stored cities are not kept in a normalized form,
25	 * mirroring {@link NamesakeCounter}. Used to drive the per-city sequence of an owner's
26	 * {@link CustomerCodeGenerator customer code}.
27	 */
28	@Component
29	public class CityOwnerCounter {
30	
31	    private final ClinicService clinicService;
32	
33	    public CityOwnerCounter(ClinicService clinicService) {
34	        this.clinicService = clinicService;
35	    }
36	
37	    /**
38	     * Counts the existing owners whose city matches the given one, case-insensitively.
39	     *
40	     * @param city the city of the owner being created
41	     * @return the number of existing owners in that city
42	     */
43	    public long count(String city) {
44	        return this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
45	            .filter(existing -> existing.getCity() != null && existing.getCity().equalsIgnoreCase(city))
46	            .count();
47	    }
48	}

19	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.service.ClinicService;
20	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
21	
22	/**
23	 * Counts how many existing owners share a given owner's name, i.e. have the same first name and
24	 * last name compared case-insensitively. The comparison is done in memory because the stored names
25	 * are not kept in a normalized form, mirroring {@link OwnerHouseholdUniquenessValidator}.
26	 */
27	@Component
28	public class NamesakeCounter {
29	
30	    private final ClinicService clinicService;
31	
32	    public NamesakeCounter(ClinicService clinicService) {
33	        this.clinicService = clinicService;
34	    }
35	
36	    /**
37	     * Counts the existing owners whose first and last name match the given ones, case-insensitively.
38	     *
39	     * @param firstName the first name of the owner being created
40	     * @param lastName  the last name of the owner being created
41	     * @return the number of existing owners sharing that first and last name
42	     */
43	    public int count(String firstName, String lastName) {
44	        return (int) this.clinicService.findAllOwners().stream()
45	            .filter(existing -> equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getFirstName(), firstName)
46	                && equalsIgnoreCase(existing.getLastName(), lastName))
47	            .count();
48	    }
49	
50	    private static boolean equalsIgnoreCase(String a, String b) {
51	        return a != null && a.equalsIgnoreCase(b);
52	    }
53	}

17	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation;
18	
19	import java.time.LocalDate;
20	
21	/**
22	 * Derives an owner's membership number, formatted {@code <customerCode>-M<YY>} where YY is
23	 * the last two digits, zero-padded, of the registration date year
24	 * (e.g. {@code SMI-0007-M26}).
25	 */
26	public final class MembershipNumberGenerator {
27	
28	    private MembershipNumberGenerator() {
29	    }
30	
31	    /**
32	     * Builds the membership number for a new owner.
33	     *
34	     * @param customerCode     the owner's customer code
35	     * @param registrationDate the owner's registration date
36	     * @return the membership number, e.g. {@code "SMI-0007-M26"}
37	     */
38	    public static String generate(String customerCode, LocalDate registrationDate) {
39	        return String.format("%s-M%02d", customerCode, registrationDate.getYear() % 100);
40	    }
41	}

The `POST /api/owners` endpoint is handled by `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`OwnerRestControllerV1.java:142-170`). Here is every validation and side-effect, in the exact order it happens:

## Before the method body
1. **Authorization gate** (`@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")`, line 142) — caller must have the `OWNER_ADMIN` role.
2. **Schema/Bean-Validation on the request body** — the incoming `OwnerFieldsDto` is bound and validated by the framework before the method runs (constraints from the OpenAPI-generated DTO, e.g. `@Size(min=1)` on fields).

## Inside `addOwner`, top to bottom
3. **Address normalization** (line 145, `AddressNormalizer.normalize`) — *side-effect on the DTO*: trims, collapses internal whitespace, upper-cases, and expands street abbreviations (`ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`). `null` stays `null`.
4. **Required-field validation** (line 146, `OwnerFieldsValidator.validateRequiredFields`) — rejects with `MissingOwnerFieldsException` if any of `firstName`, `lastName`, `address`, `city`, `telephone` is null or blank (uses the already-normalized address).
5. **Map DTO → `Owner` entity** (line 148).
6. **Telephone normalization** (line 149, `TelephoneNormalizer.normalize`) — *side-effect on owner*: strips formatting, keeps a leading `+`/country code or else assumes `+61` (dropping a single leading `0`). Throws `InvalidTelephoneException` if the result isn't `+` followed by 8–15 digits.
7. **Email normalization** (line 150, `EmailNormalizer.normalize`) — *side-effect on owner*: lower-cases the email; `null` allowed, but a present value must match the email regex or `InvalidEmailException` is thrown.
8. **Registration-date defaulting + business-day adjustment** (lines 151-152) — *side-effect on owner*: if no `registrationDate` supplied, use `LocalDate.now()` (today = 2026-09-16); then roll a Saturday/Sunday forward to the next Monday via `BusinessDayAdjuster`.
9. **Daily-registration capacity check** (line 153, `DailyRegistrationCapacityValidator`) — rejects with `DailyRegistrationLimitExceededException` if ≥ 100 owners already registered on that (business) day.
10. **Telephone uniqueness check** (line 154, `OwnerTelephoneUniquenessValidator`) — rejects with `DuplicateOwnerTelephoneException` if the normalized telephone already exists on any owner.
11. **City capacity check** (line 155, `CityOwnerCapacityValidator`) — rejects with `CityOwnerCapacityExceededException` if the city (case-insensitive) already holds ≥ 50 owners.
12. **Household handling** (lines 156-160) — branches on `sharesHousehold`:
    - **Not sharing** → `OwnerHouseholdUniquenessValidator.validateUnique` (line 157): rejects with `DuplicateOwnerHouseholdException` if another owner has the same last name + address (compared case-insensitively, whitespace-collapsed).
    - **Sharing** → `OwnerHouseholdRegistrar.assignHousehold` (line 159): *side-effects* — if a matching household exists, assigns a shared `householdId` to the new owner and **backfills + saves** existing members that lack it; if no such household, leaves the new owner without one.
13. **Namesake count** (line 161, `NamesakeCounter`) — *side-effect on owner*: sets `namesakeCount` to the number of existing owners with the same first+last name (case-insensitive).
14. **Customer-code generation** (lines 162-163, `CustomerCodeGenerator` + `CityOwnerCounter`) — *side-effect on owner*: sets `customerCode` = `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, where `NNNN` is one more than the current per-city owner count.
15. **Persist the owner** (line 164, `clinicService.saveOwner`) — *side-effect: DB insert*. On persist, JPA/Hibernate also enforces the entity constraints (`@NotEmpty` on address/city/telephone, `@Pattern` E.164 on telephone), and the entity's `@PrePersist` re-applies the business-day adjustment to `registrationDate`.
16. **Membership-number generation** (line 165, `MembershipNumberGenerator`) — *side-effect on owner, after save*: sets `membershipNumber` = `<customerCode>-M<YY>` (last two digits of the registration-date year).
17. **Build response** (lines 166-169) — map to `OwnerDto`, set `Location: /api/owners/{id}` header, return **201 Created**.

One thing worth flagging: `membershipNumber` is set *after* `saveOwner` (step 16) and is never persisted in this method, so the value appears in the returned DTO but is not written to the database on creation.
